title: Experiment ops pocket guide for crossfunc canaries (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
A compact, action-first reference for people running cross-functional canaries and AB experiments where LLM inference and routing decisions matter. Designed for: release stewards, oncall, SRE, product owners, and solutions engineers. Keep this in your mental pocket during small-batch exposures.

Quick pre-launch checklist (5 minute sprint):
- Verify feature flag exists and default path mapped to fallback model (flag id + owner).
- Smoke: 100 synthetic traces hitting new path, success rate >= 99% and mean latency within expected band.
- Observability hooks: per-slice dashboards wired (latency, 50/95/99, error-rate, token-cost, llm-quality-signal).
- Canary routing policy: percentage, cohorts, shards. Confirm no overlapping slices that will bias metrics.
- Rollback plan: exact command and owner assigned.

Steward script (what to say/do in first 15 minutes):
1) Announce via #canary-ops: "Launching slice X -> model v2 @ 09:12 PT. Steward: <name>. Observers: SRE, Product. Abort threshold TODO."
2) Start live monitor: open latency dashboard and model-quality tracker.
3) Run canary health probes every minute for first 10m (synthetic prompt set).
4) If token-cost spike or 95p latency > threshold, reduce exposure by half and notify teams.

Telemetry shortlist (minimum signals):
- User-facing latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Internal request time (proxy + model-infer)
- Model error classes (e.g., decode errors, empty responses, hallucination flags)
- Token cost per request (moving avg)
- Quality regression bucket (prompt-set pass/fail)
- Traffic composition (region, auth tier, model route)

Abort & escalation thresholds (example):
- Hard abort: p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 consecutive mins OR error-rate > 3% absolute increase from baseline for 3 mins.
- Soft throttle: p95 latency > 1.5x baseline OR token-cost uplift > 30% minute-over-minute -> reduce slice by 50%.
- Quality alert: regression on curated prompt-set where failure rate increases by >= 5% absolute -> pause and run immediate A/B comparison traces.

Quick rollback commands (examples):
- Feature flag toggle (curl):
  curl -X POST $FF_API/toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"experiment-x","state":"off"}'
- Traffic re-route (console): use 'route switch --slice X --to model-v1' or the Console quick action.

Minimal canary experiment anatomy (recommended):
- Seeded cohort (0.5% of traffic) -> hold 10m
- Synthetic probe cadence: 1/min
- Observability warm window: 5m
- Expand step: x2 exposure every 20m while checks pass (max 8x)
- Manual gating at product-stakeholder signoff points (important for behavioral changes)

Communication templates (copy/paste and adapt):
- Launch: "[LAUNCH] slice X -> model-v2 at 09:12 PT. Steward: Aisha P. Watch latency & cost. If p99 > 2x baseline or errors rise > 3ppt, abort and notify #canary-ops."
- Abort notice: "[ABORT] Pausing exposure for slice X @ 09:24 PT. Reason: p99 latency spike to 3x baseline. Rolling back to model-v1 and investigating. Oncall: Riley C."
- Post-check-in (15m): "Canary update: exposure 0.5% -> 1.0%. No quality regressions observed on seed-set. Next expand 09:40 PT if stable."

Small A/B tips for LLMs:
- Keep A and B consistent in prompt encoding and client-side truncation to avoid hidden biases.
- Use deterministic decoding for evaluation traces where possible (top-k 1, fixed seed) to isolate behavior differences.
- Maintain a stable small prompt-set (30-100) representing high-risk user journeys — run every probe.
- Watch for class imbalance in A/B samples (region, tier) and weight appropriately.

Runbook snippets for oncall (fast checklist):
- If alert fires: 1) identify slice and time window, 2) check synthetic probe log for pattern, 3) reduce exposure to 0 if severe, 4) collect traces + open incident thread, 5) assign owner to triage.

Notes to self / unresolved questions (actions):
- Add automated rollback hook in Console for p99-based aborts (PR owner: Miguel).
- Decide: should cost-buckets trigger auto-throttle for paid tiers only? (Product decision)
- Build a tiny mobile-only slice to validate edge-network latency separately.

Appendix: quick synthetic probe example (curl):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"model-v2","prompt":"Summarize: The user asked for the weather in Paris. Expected: concise weather summary.","max_tokens":40}' | jq -r '.choices[0].text'

If anything here is unclear, ping me (Aisha) or leave a note in this doc. This is intentionally terse — copy these snippets into incident checklists and into the oncall pager runbook.

Last edited notes: initial draft with field-tested heuristics from 4 crossfunc canaries in Q2-Q3 2025. Intend to merge into the formal playbook after two more dry runs.
